memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. The record's judgement: Fortum is a recovery with a contracting option attached, priced as a structural growth story, and at 23.62 EUR (2026-10-02) the modal total shareholder return is about 0.3 percent a year over eighteen months and 3.0 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar. The park rule's gate is not triggered (management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability A); the case is parked on the return, not on the gate. Not invalidated, because the recovery underneath is real and the clearing price on the modal path, about 18 EUR, is a price the stock has traded at within the last twelve months. What would re-open it: the price near 18 EUR with the thesis intact; or a second PPA of 100 MW or more announced with the 2027-2028 Nordic forward curve above EUR 52/MWh, which would move 'Investment Setup' to 'Demand Inflection' at B and the 'Modal return' to a C or B from a lower starting multiple. Direction of the judgement firm; the odds on a second PPA (45 percent by 2028-04-02) are the soft part.
case: - The thesis: a recovery with a contracting option attached, priced as a structural growth story; at 23.62 EUR the shares already pay for the volume recovery, the September curve, the Google contract and part of a second one.

- The change that is real is a recovery, not growth. Comparable EPS 1.28 EUR (FY2023) to 0.82 EUR (FY2025) on nuclear outages, dry hydrology and lower hedge prices; own cycle troughed Q3 2025 at comparable operating profit 97 EURm; H1 2026 comparable operating profit 627 EURm, +8.6 percent; hydro +19 percent in Q2 2026; nuclear availability 75 percent against 90 percent so normalisation alone returns 3 to 5 TWh at near-full drop-through (EUR 150 to 250 million of sales at EUR 45 to 50/MWh). Modal FY2028 EPS 1.15 EUR below FY2023's 1.28 EUR; consensus 1.21 EUR also below; FY2023 to FY2028 compound about -2 percent a year. The parts-add-up check reconciles: revenue +8.1 percent a year, margin +2.7 percent, EBITDA +11.0 percent (1,242 to about 1,700 EURm), below-EBITDA +1.0 percent, share count 0.0 percent, product +12.1 percent against the claimed +11.9 percent.

- The one decisive new force is one contract on about 10 percent of volumes. Google proves the fleet can be sold to a hyperscaler at a premium (about EUR 80/MWh, 60 percent above the curve; about EUR 125 million pre-tax), which is why a second contract is plausible at about 45 percent odds by 2028-04-02 and probable at about 60 percent by 2029-10-02 (pipeline in steel, aluminium, hydrogen derivatives and data centres; the Google MoU; Fingrid's 5 GW; against: one contract in a year of trying, three-to-five-year industrial tenors, Microsoft's exclusion, the forty-fold tax rise). It does not change the price of the other 90 percent: 80 percent of rest of 2026 at EUR 40/MWh, 65 percent of 2027 at EUR 41/MWh, below the FY2025 achieved EUR 51.4/MWh.
counter_case: - At 'Investment Thesis': the bull case at its strongest. The Nordic balance tightens from 2027 as wind additions fall below 500 MW a year while Fingrid's 5 GW of data-centre connection agreements and Google's EUR 13 billion of Finnish investment convert into load; the 2027-2028 curve moves to EUR 55 to 60/MWh; two or three more hyperscaler contracts follow the Google blueprint within twelve months, taking contracted output towards the 25 percent at which, in Deutsche Bank's words, wholesale price dependency falls dramatically; FY2028-FY2029 EPS runs to 1.40 to 1.55 EUR; the market keeps paying 20 times for a clean, contracted, growing baseload fleet; the shares reach EUR 30 to 33, Morgan Stanley's bull, 26 percent a year. The evidence for it is exactly what the momentum readings carry: estimates up 17 to 25 percent in three months at FY2027-FY2028, a Stage 2 price with relative strength at the 85th percentile, a sell-side that moved from Sell to Hold and Buy within a fortnight of the contract. The record concedes: the direction of every short-term indicator is the bull's; the Google terms are better than anyone modelled; if a second PPA of 100 MW or more is signed within six months, the stock very likely holds 20 times through the eighteen-month horizon. The record holds because the bar is 20 percent a year and the bull branch needs two conditions, a second PPA and a sustained EUR 58/MWh curve, with joint odds of 15 to 20 percent (options market 9.4 percent for EUR 33); because the research that looked hardest for failure modes found the false friend, a landmark contract read as fleet-wide pricing, the most consistent profile; because the broker that likes the long-term story best rates the shares Hold at EUR 25, fairly valued at 20 times 2027; and because the modal clearing price of about 18 EUR is where Morgan Stanley's bear case and DNB Carnegie's base DCF sit. Where the bull wins: the Q4 2026 hedge book showing 2027-2028 realisations above EUR 42/MWh and a second announcement by end-Q1 2027.

- At 'Foundations': the asset deserves a B. Perpetual water rights, 4.7 GW of hydro with storage across seasons, weeks and hours, 3.3 GW of nuclear licensed to 2050 at 11 to 16 g CO2/kWh, grid access on twelve powered-land sites with 5 GW, leverage 1.4 times, BBB+ stable, and an operator who just proved the fleet can be sold to a hyperscaler for 22 years at a 60 percent premium; wind experts call this baseload increasingly valuable; Google chose it over new renewables; on this view the merchant exposure is the opportunity because a tightening balance lifts every uncontracted megawatt-hour. The record concedes the asset and holds at C because robustness here means the price of the output: EBITDA fell from 1,903 EURm to 1,240 EURm over FY2023 to FY2025 while the moat was unchanged; the same regulators that grant licences have taxed windfalls and cancelled bonuses; the same hyperscalers have excluded existing nuclear; the krona is unhedged. Where it wins: a second and third PPA taking contracted output towards 25 percent.
triggers: - Re-open the case: price near 18 EUR with the thesis intact; or a second PPA of 100 MW or more with the 2027-2028 curve above EUR 52/MWh.

- Achieved power price (Key Driver): Alarm below EUR 42/MWh on the 2027-2028 curve; Invalidate below EUR 38/MWh sustained; confirm above EUR 42/MWh; the review's premium-multiple condition is the curve holding above EUR 52/MWh through the winter; management must show 2027-2028 hedged realisations above EUR 42/MWh in the Q4 2026 hedge book (late January 2027).

- Second PPA (Key Driver): Alarm if none by end-Q1 2027; Invalidate if none by end-2027 with the chief executive's pipeline language softening; the earnings review's test is two PPAs of 100 MW or more by end-Q1 2027.

- Nuclear availability and hydrology (Key Driver): Alarm if 2027 nuclear guidance is below 24 TWh; Invalidate on a third consecutive year below 85 percent availability; watch Oskarshamn 3 after the 2026-07-10 restart, Olkiluoto 2's rotor limit at 82.6 percent ending with the 2027 outage, Nordic reservoirs against the 84 TWh baseline and the ten-year average.
- The multiple (Key Driver): Alarm below 17.5 times, the end of the theme trade.

- Premium compression by batteries (Key Risk): Alarm if the 2026 premium prints below EUR 8/MWh; bear case EUR 5 to 6/MWh by 2027-2028; magnitude EUR 1 to 2/MWh on about 42 TWh, EUR 40 to 90 million of operating profit.
